findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "triage" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: no_arguments_triage_this_hosts_own_crawler_log, triage_my_request, whoami, example, triage_log · Private data: no_arguments_triage_this_hosts_own_crawler_log, triage_my_request, whoami, example, robots_from_log · Public sink: no_arguments_triage_this_hosts_own_crawler_log, triage_my_request, whoami, example, summarize_by_operator · Destructive: no_arguments_triage_this_hosts_own_crawler_log, whoami, example, find_impersonators.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: no_arguments_triage_this_hosts_own_crawler_log, triage_my_request, whoami, example, triage_log · Private data: no_arguments_triage_this_hosts_own_crawler_log, triage_my_request, whoami, example, robots_from_log · Public sink: no_arguments_triage_this_hosts_own_crawler_log, triage_my_request, whoami, example, summarize_by_operator · Destructive: no_arguments_triage_this_hosts_own_crawler_log, whoami, example, find_impersonators

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "find_impersonators" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
